conventions.convention: Remapping uses exact Lebesgue intersection measures between finite measurable partitions up to null sets, with positive cell volumes; approximate clipping weights are separate data.
Curved maps preserve orientation, extend to neighborhood diffeomorphisms, have certified positive Jacobians, and agree across shared reference facets under affine facet identification.

Geometry errors e0 and e1 are respectively uniform map-value and operator-norm derivative differences on a common reference domain; the Laplace tensor is J DΦ⁻¹DΦ⁻ᵀ. Boundary lifting and data errors remain separate.

The nodal conformity result concerns real H2 ∩ H1_0 functions on the square (-1,1)² and explicitly assumes AC and Countable Choice; boundary values are established from the closure-defined Sobolev space.

Clipping normalizes polygon cycles counterclockwise, retains boundary points using nonnegative orientation signs, clears a common positive denominator for predicate calls, and uses exact rational crossing arithmetic.

The refinement guarantee is restricted to the square and the shear Φ(x,y)=(x,y+x²/4), with compatible diagonal-reference labels, persistent binary-path identifiers, three-generation uniform requests, and transactional budget retries.

load_bearing.statement: An admissible curved cell is the image of a closed reference simplex under a C2 map extending to an orientation-preserving neighborhood diffeomorphism, with positive Jacobian and bounded derivative, inverse derivative, and second derivative; neighboring maps have matching facet traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Under the finite partition hypotheses of def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping, exact overlap remapping of source piecewise constants is the L2 orthogonal projection onto target piecewise constants, is L2 contractive, preserves total mass, and preserves nonnegativity.

Assume Countable Choice. On a matching shape-regular affine triangulation of [-1,1]², the nodal P1 approximation of Φ(x,y)=(x,y+x²/4) satisfies e0 ≤ Ch² and e1 ≤ Ch; for sufficiently small h its Jacobian is at least 1/2 and the approximate map is globally injective.

For the orientation-preserving geometry maps with Jacobians at least j* > 0 and uniformly bounded derivatives, the Laplace tensor gap is bounded by Ce1, and the associated bilinear-form defect is bounded by Ce1 times the two L2 gradient norms.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. For a finite matching triangular mesh of (-1,1)² and real u ∈ H2 ∩ H1_0, the cellwise continuous representatives give consistent vertex values; the global nodal P1 interpolant is continuous, vanishes on boundary edges, and belongs to H1_0.

Recursive reference-edge closure of a compatible labeled reference triangulation terminates in a matching conforming affine descendant; a common injective geometry map with matching facet traces produces matching curved interfaces.

Assume Countable Choice. For the stated continuous cellwise-C1 maps on the reference square and common C2 physical lift G, the H1-dual norm of the pullback-gradient residual is at most 2(L1e1 + ML2e0).

concerns.concern: Statement, line 30: “The surface Jacobian agrees with the Gram-metric factor in [[def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map]].” The cited definition allows an arbitrary reference facet parametrization, whereas proof step 1.2 establishes this equality using an orthonormal tangent matrix T. For A=I in dimension two, unit normal (0,1), and reference facet chart f(t)=(2t,0), the defined cofactor surface Jacobian is 1, while the cited chart Gram factor is 2. The unqualified equality therefore fails; the reference-chart area factor must be distinguished from the relative surface Jacobian.

Statement, line 34 contains literal backslash-n text immediately before the displayed estimate and immediately before “where” (the source reads “then\n$$” and “$$\nwhere”). These are serialized newline escapes rather than actual layout newlines.

alerts.finding: Definition, line 27: “Let $\mathbb D=\{m2^e:m,e\in\mathbb Z\}$ be its dyadic subfield.” This set is not a field: it contains 3 but not 1/3, since 3m2^e=1 has no integer m,e. The actual dyadic-coordinate algorithms use this set, so the displayed set and its asserted field classification disagree.
